procedure: Validate replay capture pins and strict-base64 decoded body hashes/lengths; decode saved body as strict UTF8.
Parse original HTML independently with Python HTMLParser; select source pre blocks by document/unique-main scope, not by emitted classes or ranges.
Pair all selected source pre blocks, structured pre nodes and Markdown fences in source order; require exact block counts and cleaned-text equality for every pair.
Decode entities, normalize CR/CRLF and Cc/Cf escapes, remove exactly one immediate initial source-pre LF where present, and count half-open UTF16 offsets.
Independently reconstruct every eligible full pre/code class and span.boring/emphasis source range and compare complete ordered entry arrays for both saved output formats.
Require exact Markdown payload equality after removing recorded container indentation and allowing only the serializer's single terminal LF for non-LF-terminated code.
Record every source opening tag/location, expected/emitted association, exact associated slice, text digest, all failures, and beginning/end input hashes.
limitations: Python HTMLParser is not an HTML5 tree builder or namespace engine; pre-local repair/foreign/hidden cases are rejected rather than silently approximated.
Unique-main/document selection is checked for these saved pages, not a general reimplementation of content-focus or visibility policies.
Source line-number removal is not modeled; candidate gutters are reported and prevent passing without further analysis.
Exact source-text/ordered-pre mapping establishes associations for these captures, not original native numeric-ID identity or general selection completeness.
No server authentication, live freshness, CSS rendered visibility, compiler meaning, runtime behavior, or executable acceptance is established.
